question: Locate the anchor function for the request_payload field in the console.log object whose action is request.transform after entering the request draft, clicking Parse Draft, selecting restricted in #policySelect, selecting expedite in #prioritySelect, clicking Stage Envelope, checking #sealRequest, clicking Queue Transform, and clicking Release Request. The anchor function is the first target-specific request-payload value constructor on the dynamic behavior chain: after form reads, draft snapshot caching, stage-envelope construction, queue-envelope construction, release routing, request normalization, tuple packing, asynchronous scheduling, and runtime configuration selection, its function body itself constructs the target observable request payload object with method, endpoint, headers, and body. It is not merely collecting input, parsing the draft, generating an internal request ticket, forwarding control, wrapping a return value, or outputting to console. Return exactly one complete function as a single JSON object matching answer_format.response_schema. Do not return generic utilities, event handlers, the full call chain, internal ticket-only helpers, shadow emitters, or the final sink. Note: you may only inspect code under captures; the full codebase is not accessible.
anchor_definition_general: A function is target-specific with respect to the observable above if at least one statement in its body constructs or binds the target value, writes the target field, or dispatches the target action, and removing that statement would break the observed output under the prescribed interaction. A function is generic if it is a reusable utility (hash/encode/serialize/normalize/collect-features), a control-flow dispatcher (router/interceptor-pipeline/event-bus/scheduler), or a preparation routine (validate input/collect UI state/lifecycle hook) whose body would look the same regardless of which behavior it currently serves. The anchor is the unique target-specific function on the chain whose immediate caller is generic, i.e. the shallowest target-specific function on the path from the trigger to the sink. If a target-specific function C is called by a generic dispatcher B and itself calls a generic utility D (e.g. a hash routine), the anchor is C, not B and not D. If a generic function A merely writes whatever its callee B returns into the target field, and B is dedicated to computing that value, the anchor is B. If the target-specific statement is one branch inside a larger function F that also handles unrelated cases, F is still a valid anchor candidate.
anchor_worked_example: Worked example (different scenario, illustration only): a checkout page emits body.order_sig_v2 after the user clicks Submit Order. The chain is: click Submit Order -> construct order draft (generic prep) -> encode checkout state (generic prep) -> collect async profile receipt (generic prep) -> compose request envelope (generic prep) -> run interceptor pipeline (generic dispatcher) -> select sealing interceptor (ANCHOR) -> canonicalize payload fields (nested helper) -> fold payload with receipt and pepper (nested helper) -> compute digest (generic SHA-256 core utility) -> write body.order_sig_v2 -> send request (generic wrapper/sink). The sealing interceptor is the anchor: its immediate caller is the generic interceptor-pipeline dispatcher, and its own body is the highest point on the chain whose code, read alone, explains why order_sig_v2 specifically is produced. Functions below it (canonicalize, fold) are nested helpers; the digest routine is a core utility; dispatcher and sender are path/wrapper. Other same-click values such as analytics_sig or coupon_digest are off-chain decoys. Apply the same reasoning to the actual page and bundle.

function_name.description: The identifier on the function declaration line in the captured bundle slice. Use the name as it appears in captures, not a guessed source-level name.

file.description: Path to the JavaScript file under captures/ that contains the function. Must match visible_corpus.

slice.description: One contiguous source slice covering exactly one complete function body in the captured bundle.

start_line.description: 1-based inclusive start line of the function in file.

end_line.description: 1-based inclusive end line of the function in file.

start_offset.description: 0-based byte offset in file where the function slice begins.

end_offset.description: 0-based byte offset in file where the function slice ends, exclusive.

code.description: Exact source text of the complete function from start_offset to end_offset. Must start with `function <function_name>(` and end with the closing brace of that function.

public_constraints: Only code visible under captures is in scope.
Submit exactly one JSON object matching answer_format.response_schema; do not wrap it in markdown fences unless the evaluation harness explicitly requires that.
function_name and slice.code must refer to the same function declaration in the captured bundle.
slice.code must be one complete function with balanced braces, not a signature fragment, partial body, or multiple functions.
Return one top-1 function, not a list of candidate chains.
Do not return the final console sink.

Constrain the observable by both action (request.transform) and field (request_payload).
The payload endpoint changes when policy changes.
The payload body changes when the request draft changes.
The payload headers and body change when the seal checkbox changes.
Similar values printed by console.debug or console.info are distractors.
notes: Use the page behavior and the console output as the starting point.
Only the value printed by console.log with action request.transform is the target.
Changing policy from restricted to standard changes the target endpoint.
Changing the draft file name changes the target body.
Checking or unchecking Seal Request before Queue Transform changes the target payload.
The same input and request configuration should produce the same target payload.
